---
title: "Testing Terminal UI Applications in R"
description: "Use termr's headless driver to simulate keyboard input and inspect rendered terminal output in deterministic R application tests."
---

`test_app()` starts a termr application with a headless driver. Input is
queued, time is simulated, and output passes through the normal event loop
and renderer into a virtual terminal. Tests can inspect widget state and
visible output without taking over a real terminal.

## A complete keyboard and screen test

[Install termr](getting-started.html#install-termr), save the following chunk
as `greeting-test.R`, and run `Rscript greeting-test.R`. Only termr and base R
are needed. This is the canonical headless testing recipe; it also executes
as part of the website build.

```{r greeting-test}
library(termr)

application <- app(
  vertical(
    label("Name"),
    input(id = "name"),
    button("Greet", id = "greet"),
    label("", id = "result")
  ),
  on("button.pressed", "#greet", function(event, app) {
    app$query_one("#result")$update(
      paste("Hello,", app$query_one("#name")$value)
    )
  }),
  bind("escape", "quit")
)

verify_greeting <- function() {
  pilot <- test_app(application, width = 40, height = 8)
  on.exit(pilot$stop(), add = TRUE)

  pilot$type("Ada")
  pilot$press("tab", "enter")

  screen <- pilot$screen_text()
  stopifnot(identical(pilot$query_one("#result")$text, "Hello, Ada"))
  stopifnot(any(grepl("Hello, Ada", screen, fixed = TRUE)))
  screen
}

verified_screen <- verify_greeting()
cat(verified_screen, sep = "\n")
```

A successful run exits with status 0. `stopifnot()` raises an error on a
failed assertion. In a testthat project, place the interaction inside a
`test_that()` block and use `expect_identical()` and `expect_true()` for
structured failure reports.

## Keep tests deterministic

- Fix the virtual terminal width and height: layout and wrapping depend on
  dimensions. `screen_text()` returns one string per row.
- `type()` sends text to the focused widget. Use `focus("#name")` when an
  application has several inputs; `press()` takes names such as `"tab"` and
  `"enter"`.
- Use `advance(seconds)` for simulated timers and `resize(width, height)`
  for layout checks. Background workers run real processes and need separate
  waiting and timeout checks; they are not simulated by the headless clock.
- Always stop the pilot. A helper function with `on.exit()` cleans up even
  when an assertion fails.
- Screen snapshots can complement state assertions. Inspect diffs before
  accepting changed snapshots.

Headless tests cover application behavior and rendering. They do not establish
real terminal input, escape handling or cleanup on every host. See the
[platform validation matrix](https://github.com/menshikovs/termr/blob/main/docs/platform-testing.md)
for terminal checks and limitations.
